problems.title: Render outer glows in layered PSDs
problems.summary: Keep a layer’s glow visible when an open-source renderer rebuilds the image.
problems.context: A PSD stores layers and can also store a finished preview. The psd-tools issue tracks a gap where rebuilt images can lose the Outer Glow effect that appears in the preview. A small test file would let different tools compare their rendering.
problems.task: Create a tiny PSD with one original shape and an Outer Glow layer effect. Add a reference PNG and a second PSD with the glow off. Record the versions and commands you used to render them.
problems.review: Another person can recreate the comparison. Show the alpha and color falloff outside the shape, quantify the difference from the reference, and confirm the no-glow control stays clear.

problems.title: Give each transit feed notice an agency
problems.summary: Help operators see which findings in a shared timetable belong to them.
problems.context: A single GTFS feed can serve more than one operator. A combined validation report makes it harder for each agency to find the notices it can act on. MobilityData is discussing how to attribute notices to agencies.
problems.task: Build a tiny synthetic feed with two agencies and draft the shape of a per-agency report. Include at least one notice that involves the whole feed.
problems.review: Show the fixture and command. The expected report assigns each attributable finding to the right agency and handles feed-wide findings explicitly.

problems.title: P versus NP
problems.summary: If an answer is quick to check, is there always a quick way to find it?
problems.context: The Clay Mathematics Institute lists P versus NP as a Millennium Prize Problem. A shared library of small, clearly specified reductions can help readers examine the ideas used in attempted solutions.
problems.task: Write a small Lean formalization of an existing reduction, such as 3-SAT to CLIQUE, or improve a documented lemma in a current public formalization effort. State the precise claim you are proving.
problems.review: Pin the repository and toolchain. Supply the theorem, build command, and result. Use no new axioms or unfinished proofs. State exactly what the result implies for the broader question.

sources.title: Clay Mathematics Institute, P versus NP

problems.title: Join two messy datasets without a formula
problems.summary: Make a common data-cleaning operation easier to inspect and repeat.
problems.context: An open OpenRefine proposal asks for a clearer way to join data across projects. Duplicate keys and unmatched rows are where a seemingly simple join can produce misleading results.
problems.task: Create two small CSVs with a duplicate key, a missing match, and fields someone might want to keep. Prototype how a person selects keys and fields and previews the result.
problems.review: Publish the input and expected output. Show how duplicates and unmatched rows are represented and how the choices could be recorded in project history for replay.

problems.title: Share a link to a single manuscript page
problems.summary: Open a digitized book at the page someone actually meant to share.
problems.context: IIIF Content State describes a portable way to open an object at a particular place. Mirador tracks support for importing that state. A single-page example is a small, useful piece of the wider proposal.
problems.task: Choose an openly accessible IIIF manifest and create a Content State link for one page. Prototype loading it in a fresh Mirador session.
problems.review: Publish the manifest and target canvas URLs. Show that a new session selects the intended page. Include what happens when the manifest or canvas identifier is invalid.

problems.title: Which Phoenix neighborhoods stay hottest after sunset?
problems.summary: Compare observed land-surface heat across neighborhoods using public satellite data.
problems.context: NASA’s ECOSTRESS captures land-surface temperature at different times of day. Phoenix has published a tree-canopy study layer. This is a proposed analysis of how nighttime surface temperature and canopy vary across the city.
problems.task: Choose clear scenes that cover Phoenix, document their local acquisition times, and join quality-filtered temperatures to tracts and the public tree-canopy layer.
problems.review: Publish scene IDs, quality masks, a tract-level table, and coverage and missingness. Repeat with a different scene or coverage threshold, and explain how your conclusion depends on the choice.

sources.title: City of Phoenix tree-canopy study layer

problems.title: Make browser subtitle tests repeatable
problems.summary: Check timed text without letting a moving playhead change the comparison.
problems.context: Web Platform Tests tracks a WebVTT snapshot mismatch. Native controls can display different playback states when the screenshots are taken at different moments.
problems.task: Contribute a test fixture that seeks to a fixed playback time and waits for the intended cue before capture. Run it repeatedly in two browser engines.
problems.review: Include the test command, engine versions, and representative artifacts. The target cue is present during the expected time and repeated captures have stable relevant content.

problems.title: Make a historic newspaper page searchable
problems.summary: Correct one column from a public scan and record exactly what changed.
problems.context: The Library of Congress is reprocessing Chronicling America to improve searchable text. Public scans and word-level machine transcriptions make it possible to document improvements page by page.
problems.task: Choose one column on a pre-1920 page. Create a TSV with stable line references, the original OCR, corrected text, and flags for uncertain readings.
problems.review: Link the original scan and machine text. A second reader can compare every line with the source image and identify remaining uncertainty.

problems.title: Build a test set for overlapping galaxies
problems.summary: Create a small public benchmark from released catalogs and telescope images.
problems.context: Images of overlapping galaxies are useful for studying dust. Galaxy Zoo has published accepted and rejected candidate catalogs, and the Legacy Surveys provide public image cutouts.
problems.task: Build an independent manifest of 20 accepted and 20 rejected coordinates from the released catalogs. Use a documented scale and release for their image cutouts.
problems.review: Include the input releases, coordinates, source labels, cutout locations, and excluded records. Publish enough code to reproduce the selection and summarize ambiguities in the labels.

problems.title: The Hodge conjecture
problems.summary: Identify which topological features of algebraic varieties come from algebraic cycles.
problems.context: The Clay Mathematics Institute lists the Hodge conjecture as a Millennium Prize Problem. Concrete examples can help distinguish cases where a statement is already known from the general conjecture.
problems.task: Work through a known low-dimensional case or explicit projective example. Identify the relevant rational cohomology class, give a candidate algebraic cycle, and explain how their relationship is checked.
problems.review: Cite the exact theorem used and state its hypotheses. A second reader can follow the calculation, reproduce any computations, and identify the limits of the example.
